forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: Drought is the main establishment threat to planted stands in this pool: on a Spanish dryland reforestation project mortality tracked the drought index and rose further in an exceptional drought, a review links high outplanted-seedling mortality on hot, dry sites to low soil water and high temperature, and novel drought is credited with complete restoration failure even with outplanting [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_1, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_3, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_2]. In tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, native-species plantings without mulch had low survival (5.5%), and the authors advise against planting without mulching [ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: In Australia a short dry spell at planting, after soils had been saturated, did not significantly affect survival [ev_drought_hazard_preece23_1]. Apart from a single Mexican field study, whose survival figure applies to unmulched plantings and does not isolate drought [ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1], all evidence comes from high-income or unspecified settings, the complete-failure claim comes from a perspective piece not specific to forests, and the Spanish study shows technical choices interacting with drought.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge tree planting in Uganda and dune stabilisation and afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1577_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: These are compiler ratings from just these technology sheets, not measurements of storm damage to plantings, and the Turkmenistan case is a desert dune setting outside the low-income target [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm].

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: A study of reforestation in tropical developing countries lists uncontrolled fires, with uncontrolled grazing, weed competition and cutting for fuel, fodder and timber, among the main causes of reforestation failure [ev_fire_hazard_le12_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: This is a single narrative statement that does not separate fire from the non-climatic causes or quantify the damage.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Australia, flooding rains that followed Cyclone Yasi flooded newly planted plots and drowned most saplings, and a perspective on restoration notes that a record drought followed by a year of heavy rain and flooding can cause high seedling mortality [ev_flood_hazard_preece23_1, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_3].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The compiler for floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan rates the technology as coping well with river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1509_2011_general_river_flood], so flood-adapted species and sites change the picture. The literature units are narrative from high-income or unspecified settings and the perspective piece is not specific to forests.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: Outplanted seedlings on open restoration sites are exposed to air at seedling height 10 °C hotter than at 2 m, with soil or litter surfaces up to 30 °C hotter, which causes heat stress, and even minutes of extreme heat can cause seedling mortality in many species [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_2, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is review-level and from western North America or unspecified settings, with the perspective piece not specific to forests; the microclimate effect arises after the overstorey is removed by harvest or fire.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for community protection of microbasins through reforestation in Honduras judges it to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of landslide damage to planted stands [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide].

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Brazilian restinga, total mortality of planted seedlings over four years did not differ significantly between seasonally flooded depressions and dry sandbanks [ev_establishment_survival_loureiro21_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: This is a single site study in a sandy coastal plain, and both habitats had substantial mortality, so the null finding concerns the added effect of seasonal flooding only.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: On a Spanish dryland reforestation project, windstorms blew away tree shelters, and in Brazilian restinga strong constant wind breaks branches and damages planted seedlings, directly affecting height growth [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1, ev_climate_shock_loureiro21_1]. The Cabo Verde compiler judges afforestation as not coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1523_2011_local_windstorm]. In central Vietnam typhoon damage is a continuing concern for smallholder plantations and leads planters to favour short-cycle rotations [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: Compilers for afforestation in Turkmenistan and Uganda and reforestation in Honduras judge coping with windstorms or cyclones as good or moderate [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1529_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1577_2013_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_tropical_storm]. The Spanish losses were partly attributed to poor tethering, the Brazilian statement cites earlier work, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements. The Vietnam evaluation adds that the typhoon risk has so far not discouraged smallholders from continuing to plant [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1].

forest_restoration__active_planting__bio.mechanism: Planted stands create habitat and attract seed dispersers: beneath framework-species plantings in northern Thailand a range of tree seedling species recruited naturally, most of them animal-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate dune afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan as raising plant, habitat and animal diversity, citing snakes, lizards and turtles returning [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity].
forest_restoration__active_planting__bio.conditionality: Agreement is split: an INRAE expert synthesis finds that plantations generally reduce biodiversity or shift composition away from native species, citing a 40% loss of local species richness relative to uncut forest, and its own small meta-analysis gives an imprecise estimate whose interval spans zero [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]; a pantropical review warns that where forests can regenerate naturally, tree planting can reduce biodiversity benefits if the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]. The negative findings come from temperate and boreal harvest-renewal settings where the comparator is natural regeneration or uncut forest rather than degraded land, while the positive side rests on compiler ratings and a case study without an unplanted control.

forest_restoration__active_planting__car.mechanism: Planting native trees on former pasture in Brazil's Atlantic Forest built up carbon stocks of 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 Mg/ha in successively older plantings, against 138.94 Mg/ha in mature forest [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3]; a global review puts removal rates for planted forests and woodlots at 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2/ha/yr over the first 20 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1]. Soil carbon also rises: afforestation of cropland raised soil organic carbon stocks by 26% on average and tropical transitions to plantation gained 0.919% of initial soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_2], and WOCAT compilers in Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Eritrea, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate above- or below-ground carbon as increased.
forest_restoration__active_planting__car.conditionality: Soil gains are conditional: on pastures (3%) and natural grasslands the change was not significant, boreal sites lost 1.5% while other zones gained 7 to 17%, low-clay soils showed no change, and heavily disturbed site preparation cut the gain to 4% against 19% with low disturbance [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_9]; that meta-analysis draws mostly on high-income temperate sites. The planted-forest removal range includes commercial eucalyptus, teak and pine woodlots, the modelled plantation figure of 44.6 tC/ha counts harvested wood products and is a discounted present value [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2], young Brazilian plantings held only 15.7 to 27.6% of reference-forest biomass, and soil organic carbon enters this row as a component proxy.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: Planting costs come from seedling production, soil preparation and planting labour: tree planting with soil preparation is cited at US$1,400 to 34,000/ha [ev_project_cost_crouzeilles17_1], and in Tabasco, Mexico, semi-mechanised planting with a tractor-drawn plough cost US$178/ha against US$217/ha by hand [ev_project_cost_keyes97_1, ev_project_cost_keyes97_2]. Modelled plantation costs across low- and middle-income countries have a median of US$3,729/ha including replanting after harvest cycles [ev_project_cost_busch24_2], while reported establishment costs run from planting in the Masoala corridors of Madagascar to native-species reforestation in Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica and to WOCAT afforestation sheets in Honduras and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: Most figures carry no stated price year, the Mexican costs are historical field costs that exclude donated seedlings, and the Bukoski median is a modelled value; WOCAT costs are compiler-entered and converted from local-currency amounts. The pool mixes high-income (Chile, Costa Rica), upper-middle and low-income settings, and only the Honduras and Madagascar entries fall in the low and lower-middle income band.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: The abatement cost of plantation reforestation combines implementation cost, the opportunity cost of land and carbon accumulated, net of revenue from selling harvested wood products, giving a modelled median of US$23.00 per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_busch24_4].
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: This is a single modelled estimate with a wide interdecile range, from US$-14.80 (plantations profitable without carbon payments) to US$724 per tCO2, so the figure is a screening value rather than a project budget, and it depends on wood-product revenue that a restoration (non-harvest) planting would not earn.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: In a mulching experiment in tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, polyethylene mulch cut the cost of each established plant, including nursery costs, from 18.00 USD on bare soil to 2.45 USD, because 92 of 180 plants established against 10 of 180 without mulch [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. The saving comes from survival: the mulch costs money, but far more plants establish, so the cost per surviving plant falls.
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: Organic mulches lowered cost per established plant much less, to 12.50 USD with alfalfa straw and 13.33 USD with leaf litter [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. This row rests on one experiment at one tropical dry forest site, with costs in USD and no wider cost comparison, so the figures indicate the direction of the saving rather than a transferable value.

forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.mechanism: The only unit is a regional model linking large-scale reforestation in water-insecure parts of the Asia-Pacific to fewer extremely dry months in 9 of 15 regions [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.conditionality: This is a single modelled source at landscape scale in which most regional changes were not significant and one basin moved in the adverse direction; it says nothing about plot-scale planting or about measured drought impacts on rural livelihoods [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].

forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.mechanism: In a regional coupled land-climate model, reforestation reduced the probability of extremely dry months in 9 of 15 Asia-Pacific regions, especially where it also increased total annual precipitation [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.conditionality: This rests on a single modelling study of full reforestation potential at landscape scale, not on observed project outcomes; the source's table shows most regional changes were not significant, so the direction is indicative only.

forest_restoration__active_planting__fir.mechanism: The Uganda tree-planting compiler rates fire risk as unchanged, commenting that dense forest brings fire risk that is common in the neighbouring Kiruhura district but not yet a problem in Rubagano [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__active_planting__fir.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating, and its comment implies fire risk may rise as planted canopy closes rather than fall. No measured evidence on planting and fire is in the pool.

forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.mechanism: Catchment models in Slovakia and Luxembourg show afforestation lowering flood peaks, in Slovakia by about 24% on average for a large forest increase, more for short storms than long ones, and an earlier scenario converting all arable land in a basin to forest cut peak flow by 42.3% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. Compilers rate afforestation with hillside terracing in Eritrea, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan, and afforestation in Cabo Verde, Uganda and Bosnia and Herzegovina as reducing downstream flooding or flood impacts [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.conditionality: Much of the weight comes from high-income temperate catchment models at landscape scale, so transfer to low-income settings is weak [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. The remaining units are practitioner ratings, the Eritrea technology bundles planting with terracing, the Bosnia and Herzegovina compiler rates only a slight reduction, and the Honduras compiler rates no downstream change yet [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding].

forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.mechanism: Adding forest to a catchment lowers flood peaks: in the Hornad watershed of Slovakia a reforestation scenario cut the simulated peak discharge by 12% and peak flows by about 24% on average for synthetic storms, and a cited Alzette basin study in Luxembourg found an 8% reduction [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. WOCAT compilers rate flood impacts as reduced for Tugai floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan and for afforestation in Eritrea, Uganda, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.conditionality: The effect shrinks for long storms (29% for the shortest rain duration, 17% for the longest) and the quantified evidence comes from models of large land-cover changes in high-income temperate basins, well beyond project scale [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3]. The Honduras compiler rates no effect yet, expecting flood reduction only in the long term [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding], and the low-income evidence is practitioner ratings, the Eritrea sheet combining planting with hillside terracing.

forest_restoration__active_planting__pro.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate afforestation as raising fodder supply, through cut-and-carry grass in Eritrea and through planted sand-fixing species used as forage in Turkmenistan, and also in Cabo Verde; the Turkmenistan sheet also rates animal production as increased [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1330_2010_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_animal_production].
forest_restoration__active_planting__pro.conditionality: Every unit is a compiler rating rather than a measured yield, fodder is a component proxy for the production gap, and no unit reports crop yields; the Eritrea sheet combines planting with hillside terracing.

forest_restoration__active_planting__rec.mechanism: Recurrent costs are the annual maintenance of planted stands: compiler-entered maintenance for community microbasin reforestation in Honduras and for karst afforestation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and a table entry of US$775/ha per year for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wri17_11].
forest_restoration__active_planting__rec.conditionality: WOCAT figures are converted from local-currency entries by compilers and the Brazil table states no price year; only the Honduras sheet falls in the low and lower-middle income band, so the recurrent-cost picture for poorer contexts rests on a single sheet.

forest_restoration__active_planting__rur.mechanism: Planting can raise incomes through payments for environmental services and later wood sales: in Guanacaste, Costa Rica, reforestation payments made up 18.66% of beneficiaries' income during the contract and helped cover establishment and maintenance costs, alongside family employment and legal security over property [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3], and China's Sloping Land Conversion afforestation subsidies increased off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_iufro20_9]. Modelled plantations would be profitable without carbon payments across 28.3% of the feasible area [ev_economic_return_busch24_1], and WOCAT compilers rate long-term returns as positive or very positive for afforestation in Eritrea, Tajikistan, Cabo Verde, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Uganda, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Honduras. In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains for participants, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; and China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__rur.conditionality: Livelihood losses are documented: reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives [ev_household_income_le12_1], the Turkmenistan compiler reports income cut by 20 - 25% in the first 1-2 years, and the Cabo Verde sheet notes afforestation reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Most positive units are compiler ratings, income, returns and food security are proxies for poverty, and the Costa Rica evidence comes from commercial plantations under a payment scheme in a high-income setting. The Vietnam return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and the gains depended on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1], the Amazon returns are modelled for agroforestry restoration designs [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1], and the Chinese ratio counts socioeconomic outcomes only and is cited in a systematic review [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__active_planting__soi.mechanism: Tree canopy and cover intercept rainfall and reduce runoff and soil loss: in Calabria, Italy, sediment concentrations were far higher on a plot with little or no tree cover than under good eucalyptus cover [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1], and in the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation fell 55% and 78% five years after tree planting with grazing closure [ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5]. Planting on susceptible slopes reduces landslide risk and targeted reforestation in New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment could cut landslide sediment by about 20% [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]; China's reforestation programmes reduced soil erosion and sediment [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_1], and WOCAT compilers in Eritrea, Uganda, Cabo Verde, Tajikistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate soil loss as reduced. In Ethiopia, tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff depth from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2].
forest_restoration__active_planting__soi.conditionality: Plantations without understorey can increase the kinetic energy of throughfall and soil detachment [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_2], and in New Zealand erosion benefits trade off against reduced water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]. Much of the measured evidence is from high-income temperate settings, the Pakistan result combines planting with grazing closure, landslide units are recorded under erosion for lack of a landslide category, and runoff and sediment enter as components; the low-income evidence is compiler ratings apart from the Ethiopian runoff measurements [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. Similarly, an FAO–CIFOR synthesis warns of particularly serious erosion in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3].

forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate afforestation in Cabo Verde and tree planting in Uganda as reducing downstream siltation, the sediment pathway to water quality [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings, and siltation is a component proxy; no unit measures water quality directly.

forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.mechanism: In a regional land-climate model, reforestation raised water yield where added precipitation outweighed higher evapotranspiration, significantly in the Loess Plateau-North China Plain (11.4%), Yangtze Plain (16.9%), Southeast China (17.6%) and Irrawaddy (84.9%) [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]; WOCAT compilers in Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate water availability as improved.
forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.conditionality: Measured catchment evidence points the other way: young, densely spaced native-species plantations aged 25 to 45 years in the US Pacific Northwest produce dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to old growth, afforestation in New Zealand reduced water yield, and a cited review found most studies reported lower water yields, though mostly for plantation forestry [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3, ev_water_regulation_iufro18_4, ev_water_regulation_iufro18_1]. Some modelled regions show nonsignificant declines from heightened evapotranspiration [ev_water_regulation_teo22_5], the Honduras compiler sees no effect yet, and the gains are scenario outputs at landscape scale rather than project observations. A global synthesis of paired catchments found that afforestation reduced annual runoff on average by 44% when grasslands and 31% when shrublands were afforested, with proportional reductions even larger for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site, suggesting more severe effects in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]; these are afforestation of grassland and shrubland in paired catchments, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand.

forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.mechanism: The Uzbekistan compiler credits afforestation of degraded irrigated cropland with strong bio-drainage through tree transpiration [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.conditionality: The Uganda tree-planting compiler rates drainage unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_excess_water_drainage], so the strong rating rests on a single irrigated-cropland sheet. Both units are practitioner ratings.

forest_restoration__active_planting__win.mechanism: The Honduras compiler rates community reforestation of micro-basins as slightly reducing the impacts of cyclones and rain storms, by reducing landslide risk, with a greater effect expected in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__active_planting__win.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating whose explanation works through landslide risk rather than wind, so it says little about protection from cyclone winds.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.mechanism: Drought kills planted seedlings during establishment: on a dryland reforestation project in Spain mortality tracked the drought index and an exceptional severe drought worsened losses, exposing inappropriate technical measures years later, and a review attributes rising mortality of recently outplanted seedlings in dry regions to hotter and drier conditions [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_1, ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_3, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_1]. Novel drought is credited with complete restoration failure even with outplanting, and planted mangrove seedlings in Sri Lanka's higher intertidal suffered from drought and high irradiance [ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_2, ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_2]. In tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, survival of native-species plantings without mulch was low (5.5%), and the authors advise against planting without it [ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.conditionality: In Australia a short dry spell at planting did not significantly affect sapling survival, the soils having been saturated beforehand [ev_drought_hazard_preece23_1], so short dry spells at planting are not necessarily lethal. The evidence comes from high- and upper-middle-income settings with none from low- or lower-middle-income countries, the Mexican figure applies to unmulched plantings and does not isolate drought from other causes of loss [ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1], the complete-failure claim is a perspective piece covering plant restoration generally rather than forests, and the Spanish losses interact with technical choices such as tree shelters.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.mechanism: On a dryland reforestation project in Spain, plantation mortality tracked the drought index, worsened sharply in an exceptional severe drought, and that drought revealed the impact of inappropriate technical measures years later [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_1, ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_2, ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_3]. A review of hot, dry restoration sites in western North America links high seedling mortality to low soil water, high temperature and vapour-pressure deficit [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_3, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.conditionality: In Australia exposure of new plantings to a short dry spell did not significantly affect survival [ev_drought_hazard_preece23_1], so the threat depends on drought length and severity. The Spanish mortality also reflects technical decisions, and the North American units are a review citing other studies.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.mechanism: In Sri Lanka's dry and arid zones, mangrove seedlings and propagules planted in the higher intertidal suffered from drought and high irradiance, while those planted low in the intertidal of the wet zone were exposed to long submergence after heavy rains [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_2]. In tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, native-species plantings without mulch had low survival (5.5%), so the authors advise against planting without mulching [ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.conditionality: Both units point to choices that change the loss: where in the tidal frame mangroves are planted, and whether plantings are mulched [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_2, ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1]. The row rests on two single field studies; neither measures drought intensity, and the Mexican survival figure does not separate drought from other causes of mortality.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__extrem.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge planted and regenerating stands to cope well with local rainstorms: tree planting in Uganda, dune afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan, area closure in Ethiopia, assisted natural regeneration in Niger, mangrove regeneration in Senegal and broadleaf plantations with assisted regeneration in India [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1577_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1598_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1442_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__extrem.conditionality: Thunderstorms are rated as coping well for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and the Indian plantations, while hailstorms are the only storm type rated as coping only moderately, for the Indian broadleaf plantations [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4300_2019_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm]. All units are WOCAT compiler ratings, not measurements, and none describes how storm damage to young trees would occur.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__fire.mechanism: Uncontrolled fire is listed among the main causes of reforestation failure in tropical developing countries, early-successional regenerating land that is not overseen faces a high probability of fire outbreaks particularly in dry years, and young regrowth forests fail to persist partly through vulnerability to fire [ev_fire_hazard_le12_1, ev_fire_hazard_chazdon16_1, ev_establishment_survival_williams24_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__fire.conditionality: These literature units are narrative and unquantified, and they list fire alongside grazing, weeds, cutting, market shifts and perverse policies. The only rated unit, from an Indian programme where villagers actively protect the forest, judges the technology as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire], which suggests the threat depends on whether fire protection is in place.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__flood.mechanism: Floods drown young plantings: in Australia flooding rains after Cyclone Yasi drowned most saplings in newly planted plots, flooding was among the stress factors observed at all planted mangrove sites in Sri Lanka, and a drought year followed by flooding can cause high seedling mortality [ev_flood_hazard_preece23_1, ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_3, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_3]. WOCAT compilers rate an Ethiopian area closure and assisted natural regeneration in Niger as not coping well with river floods, and the Khost learning site in Afghanistan as not coping well at all with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1598_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1626_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__flood.conditionality: Other compilers rate mangrove regeneration in Senegal and floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan as coping well with river floods, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping well with storm surge, and mangrove buffers in the Philippines as coping very well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1442_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1509_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_578_2016_storm_surge_coastal_flood]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements and the literature units are narrative, so the severity of damage is not quantified; flood-adapted systems (mangroves, floodplain forest) appear more tolerant than upland closures and regeneration.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__heat_s.mechanism: On open restoration sites, outplanted seedlings sit in microsites where air at seedling height is 10 °C hotter than at 2 m and soil or litter surfaces up to 30 °C hotter, enough to cause heat stress, and even minutes of extreme heat can kill seedlings of many species [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_2, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__heat_s.conditionality: Both units are review or perspective statements citing other studies, from western North America or unspecified settings, and the perspective piece covers plant restoration generally rather than forests; no unit measures heat-driven mortality at a restoration site in a low-income country.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__landsl.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Bangladesh judges it not to cope well with landslides, and the compiler for broadleaf plantations and assisted tree regeneration in India rates it as coping moderately [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__landsl.conditionality: Community reforestation protecting microbasins in Honduras is judged to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide]. These are compiler ratings from a small set of technology sheets, not measurements, and none states how landslides damage the stands.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__sedime.mechanism: Rapid sedimentation and excess leaf litter can cause delayed mortality of mangrove trees by smothering their above-ground aerial roots [ev_establishment_survival_gijsman21_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__sedime.conditionality: This is a single review statement about existing mangrove forests, citing field and laboratory observations, not a measurement on restored stands, and it gives no magnitude.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__waterl.mechanism: In Sri Lanka, mangrove seedlings and propagules planted in the low intertidal zone of the wet zone were exposed to long-term submergence caused by heavy rains [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__waterl.conditionality: In Brazilian restinga, mortality of planted seedlings did not differ significantly between seasonally flooded depressions and dry sandbanks [ev_establishment_survival_loureiro21_1], so periodic waterlogging is not necessarily harmful. Neither source quantifies losses due to waterlogging, and the Sri Lankan case reflects poor siting along the tidal gradient.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.mechanism: Wind damages young plantings and mangrove stands: on a Spanish dryland project windstorms blew away tree shelters, strong constant wind in Brazilian restinga breaks branches and damages seedlings, mangrove tree damage rises rapidly when tropical-cyclone winds exceed 130 km/h, and extreme events can severely damage or destroy mangrove areas, making them less effective [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1, ev_climate_shock_loureiro21_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1]. WOCAT compilers judge afforestation in Cabo Verde as not coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1523_2011_local_windstorm]. In central Vietnam typhoon damage is a continuing concern for smallholder plantations and leads planters to favour short-cycle rotations [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1], and in Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have initially destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves, with frequent hurricanes changing some mangrove stands to mudflats [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.conditionality: Most other compilers judge restoration technologies in Senegal, Turkmenistan, Tunisia, Uganda, Niger and Honduras as coping well with windstorms or extratropical cyclones, and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and reforestation in Honduras as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1529_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_tropical_storm]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, the Spanish shelter losses were partly due to poor tethering, and the mangrove damage statements are cited review findings for existing forests. The Vietnam evaluation notes that the risk has so far not discouraged smallholders from continuing to plant [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1], and the Florida losses concern existing mangroves, cited in a review.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.mechanism: On a dryland reforestation project in Valencia, Spain, seedlings lost their tree shelters to windstorms and poor tethering [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1]. In Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have initially destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves, and frequent hurricanes have changed some mangrove ecosystems to mudflats [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.conditionality: The Spanish losses were partly due to poor tethering of shelters rather than wind alone [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1], and the Florida figure concerns existing mangroves and is a cited finding in a review, not a measurement on restored stands [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. The row rests on two high-income studies, neither of which measures how damage scales with wind speed.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Niger judges it to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of storm damage to regenerating stands [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm].

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler judges assisted natural regeneration as not coping well with general river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1626_2014_general_river_flood].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single practitioner judgement from a technology sheet, with no description of the damage and no measurement.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Bangladesh judges it not to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from a technology sheet; it gives no measure or description of the damage, so it is a compiler rating of how the regenerating stand copes, not a documented failure [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide].

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Compilers in Niger judge assisted natural regeneration as coping well, or moderately on agro-pastoral and pastoral land, with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1626_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_2325_2017_local_windstorm].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: Both units are practitioner judgements from Niger with no description of the damage or measurement.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Assisted regeneration recovers habitat by letting canopy cover and tree density build up: WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh rate animal and habitat diversity as increased as the habitat improved, and in Niger rate plant diversity as strongly increased where assisted natural regeneration is combined with planting selected species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity]. In Brazilian restinga, artificial perches accelerated the regeneration of native animal-dispersed species, consistent with a cited study in which perches increased seed and seedling abundance and richness [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_2].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The low-income evidence is compiler ratings without species counts, and the measured evidence comes from a single restoration site in upper-middle-income Brazil using a specific nucleation technique, so transfer to other assisted-regeneration designs is assumed.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Niger rate assisted natural regeneration as raising above-ground biomass, especially on pastoral and sylvo-pastoral land, and report a rapid increase in soil organic matter; sheets from Niger and Bangladesh also rate soil organic matter as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_2325_2017_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4372_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings with no measured carbon stocks or rates, and soil organic matter enters as a component proxy; the evidence is in context for low-income drylands and Bangladesh but has no measured backing in this row.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The costs are establishment costs per hectare entered by WOCAT compilers for assisted natural regeneration on agro-pastoral and pastoral land in Niger (US$90/ha) and in Bangladesh (US$197.62/ha), plus a table entry of US$639/ha for assisted natural regeneration in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_establishment, ev_project_cost_wri17_6].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The WOCAT values are converted by compilers from local-currency entries, the Brazil table gives no price year, and the Brazil entry is upper-middle income and so outside the low and lower-middle income range; the set is small.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler states that assisted natural regeneration on agro-pastoral, sylvo-pastoral and pastoral land, by improving vegetation cover and increasing woody production, helps reduce the impacts of long droughts during the rainy season [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The row rests on a single practitioner rating from a Niger technology sheet, with no measured drought outcome [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts].

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler reports that by improving vegetation cover and increasing woody production, assisted natural regeneration helps reduce drought impacts [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from Niger, with no measured drought outcome.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Compilers for assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh rate soil loss and surface runoff as moderately reduced, which is how this row reaches flood [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4372_2019_surface_runoff].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: No unit rates or measures downstream flooding directly; the link runs only through runoff and erosion proxies. All units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Niger rate assisted natural regeneration as increasing crop, fodder and livestock production: in the agro-pastoral zone it raised millet and sorghum production in fields, and vegetation cover on sylvo-pastoral land increased by more than 100%, lifting fodder supply [ev_crop_yield_wocat_2325_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_2325_2017_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_2325_2017_animal_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1626_2014_crop_production].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings from Niger, with no measured yields or comparison plots, and fodder enters as a component proxy for the production gap.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Recurrent costs are the annual maintenance entered by WOCAT compilers for assisted natural regeneration in Niger (US$108/ha per year) and Bangladesh (US$339.29/ha per year) [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_maintenance].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: Both values are converted by compilers from local-currency entries and come from just a pair of technology sheets.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate the long-term returns of assisted natural regeneration as positive or very positive in Niger and Bangladesh, and in Niger report that it contributes to food security and self-sufficiency in the southern regions and lowers the risk of production failure [ev_economic_return_wocat_2325_2017_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4372_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1626_2014_risk_of_production_failure].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: Every unit is a compiler rating; returns and food security are proxies for poverty, and no unit measures household income or poverty outcomes.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Niger and Bangladesh rate assisted natural regeneration as reducing surface runoff and soil loss, and the Bangladesh sheet also rates downstream siltation as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_4372_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings, with runoff and siltation entering as components; no unit measures soil loss.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Bangladesh compiler rates assisted natural regeneration as slightly reducing downstream siltation, the sediment pathway to water quality [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_4372_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single compiler rating, and siltation is a component proxy for water quality.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler rates assisted natural regeneration as slightly improving water harvesting and collection [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single compiler rating without a measured water outcome.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler rates assisted natural regeneration as lowering wind velocity, a shelter effect of regenerated woody cover [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1626_2014_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating of everyday wind speed, not of cyclone or storm damage.

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: Restoring forest on degraded land rebuilds habitat: a global meta-analysis of 221 study landscapes found forest restoration enhances biodiversity by 15-84% compared with degraded ecosystems [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1], natural regeneration outperformed active planting for plants, birds and invertebrates by 34 to 56% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], and restored mangroves support more crab production and diversity than degraded mangroves [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_1]. In the western Andes of Colombia, bird and dung beetle communities in regenerating forest resembled old growth after 15-30 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_chazdon16_1]; protecting and managing existing forest retains habitat, with community forest management in Nepal reducing deforestation and forest cover in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla rising 8% [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Niger, Bangladesh, India, Afghanistan and Turkmenistan rate diversity as increased. In Senegal's southern Groundnut Basin woody species richness rose from 27 species in a 1-year exclosure to 51 species in 5- and 12-year exclosures [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: Recovery is partial and slow: after 20 years of natural regeneration species richness reached 78% of old-growth values but composition only 33%, with recovery of composition taking about 120 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_2], and in Brazil's Atlantic Forest regaining mature-forest endemism was estimated to take 1987 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. Planting can reduce biodiversity where forests could regenerate naturally, and INRAE syntheses of mainly temperate harvest settings find plantations generally lower diversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6]; restored mangroves showed no significant difference from unvegetated tidal flats [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_2], community management transfers in Madagascar failed to halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and the Ethiopian area-closure compiler notes returning wildlife endangers crops and livestock [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The forest-cover units are a component proxy and the low-income evidence is largely compiler ratings. Governance effects are uneven: under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], an evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. These governance units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction rather than species, the Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in a systematic review, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: In low and lower-middle income settings the evidence is mainly WOCAT compiler ratings: area closure in Ethiopia brought back wildlife, assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh increased plant, animal and habitat diversity as canopy cover and tree density improved, broadleaf plantations in India provide water and habitat for small animals and birds, and protection measures in Khost, Afghanistan saw migratory animals and birds return [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity]. Community forest management across community forests in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation, retaining habitat [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: Management transfers in Madagascar remained superficial and did not stop clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and the Ethiopian compiler notes that returning wildlife became a danger to crops and domestic animals. No unit in this scope measures species directly: all biodiversity units are compiler ratings and the Nepal and Madagascar units concern forest cover, a component proxy.

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: This row rests on forest-governance evidence pooled across several countries, with forest cover standing in for habitat. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) compared with areas without payments [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]. World Bank participatory forest management projects reported reduced deforestation rates, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity where those outcomes were monitored, and Bank-supported payment schemes had a positive effect on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: The payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas, which limits what they deliver for biodiversity [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. Most units measure forest cover or deforestation, a component proxy for biodiversity, not species. The pooled payment effects come from a systematic review and meta-analysis, while the World Bank units are evaluation narratives that cover only projects that monitored outcomes; all concern keeping or managing existing forest through payments or community management rather than restoration planting.

forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.mechanism: In upper-middle income settings, regenerating forests in Colombia's western Andes came to host bird and dung beetle communities resembling old growth and suitable habitat for threatened birds [ev_biodiversity_outcome_chazdon16_1], tree species richness in Brazil's Atlantic Forest rose with time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], and artificial perches accelerated regeneration of animal-dispersed species in Brazil [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1]. Framework-species plantings in Thailand drew in naturally recruiting tree seedlings, dune afforestation in Turkmenistan is rated as raising diversity, and community forest management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla raised forest cover by 8% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1].
forest_restoration__biodiversity_priorit.conditionality: Recovery of the full community is slow: the Atlantic Forest chronosequence estimates 65 years to reach 80% animal-dispersed species and 1987 years to regain mature-forest endemism [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. The Thai case has no unplanted control, the Mexican forest-cover gain is a before-after comparison without a counterfactual and enters as a component proxy, and the Colombian result is cited from another study. In Vietnam an evaluation of grants to special-use forest management boards found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that biodiversity is hard to assess and the tracking tool used was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1].

forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.mechanism: Restoration accumulates carbon in regrowing biomass and soils: natural regeneration removes 9.1-18.8 t CO2/ha/yr in its first 20 years and planted mangroves up to 23.1 [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_3, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_2], a 20-year-old secondary forest in the moist tropics holds 51 t of above-ground carbon per hectare on average [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch19_1], and modelled 30-year carbon is higher for natural regeneration (60.2 tC/ha) than for harvested plantations (44.6 tC/ha) [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. Restored mangroves sequester more carbon than unvegetated tidal flats [ev_carbon_sequestration_su21_1], sustainable forest management sites under GEF projects sequester about 1.33 t of carbon per hectare per year more than the counterfactual [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1], and secondary regrowth in the central Amazon of Brazil reached 50% of mature forest biomass after 25 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_gehring05_1]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.conditionality: Biomass recovery is slow (about 12 decades to reach 90% of old-growth above-ground biomass) even though topsoil carbon recovers in about 5 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_poorter21_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_poorter21_1]. Afforestation soil carbon gains were not significant on pastures and grasslands and boreal sites lost 1.5% [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4], community management in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1], the modelled estimates are discounted present values or scenario potentials, and planted-forest removal factors include commercial woodlots. Soil carbon and forest cover enter as component proxies, and the low-income evidence is mostly compiler ratings. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.mechanism: In low and lower-middle income settings, WOCAT compilers rate biomass and soil carbon as increased under assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh, broadleaf plantations in India, area closure with Acacia reforestation in Tunisia, enclosures with controlled burning in Tanzania, afforestation in Eritrea and Uzbekistan, reforestation in Honduras and protection in Khost, Afghanistan [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1568_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1607_2014_biomass_above_ground_C]. Community forest management in Nepal retained forest cover by reducing deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points, and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3].
forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.conditionality: No unit in this scope measures carbon stocks or rates: the carbon units are compiler ratings, and forest cover and soil organic matter enter as component proxies. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not stop clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2]. The one unit that measures carbon directly finds no gain: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1]. Under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was also insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2]; the Indian, Bolivian and Nepal results are cited in systematic reviews.

forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.mechanism: This row rests on forest-governance evidence pooled across several countries, with forest cover standing in for carbon kept in standing forest. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]. World Bank participatory forest management projects reported reduced deforestation rates and regeneration of degraded forests where those outcomes were monitored, and Bank-supported payment schemes had a positive effect on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__carbon_sequestration.conditionality: No unit measures carbon stocks or sequestration rates: all four measure forest cover or deforestation, a component proxy. The payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The pooled payment effects come from a systematic review and meta-analysis, the World Bank units are evaluation narratives covering only projects that monitored outcomes, and all concern keeping existing forest through payments or community management rather than restoration.

forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.mechanism: Cost per hectare depends mainly on method: modelled implementation cost has a median of US$140/ha for natural regeneration against US$3,729/ha for plantations including replanting [ev_project_cost_busch24_1, ev_project_cost_busch24_2], natural regeneration methods are cited at US$12-3,880/ha against US$105-25,830/ha for restoration projects in the tropics and subtropics [ev_project_cost_williams24_2], and natural regeneration in Uganda is tabled at US$26/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_5]. Mangrove restoration costs a median of 1,097.16 USD/ha across a global meta-analysis, and community support kept mangrove reforestation in the Philippines at US$211/ha [ev_project_cost_su21_1, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_4]; the opportunity cost of land (median US$4,807/ha) is generally higher and more variable than implementation cost [ev_project_cost_busch24_5]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh gives a mean mangrove restoration cost of 7,700 USD/ha across the country [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].
forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.conditionality: Most reported figures state no price year, some are present values (Viet Nam mangroves at 843 US dollars per hectare) or assumptions (the TEEB study's assumed US$2,390-3,450/ha) rather than observed costs [ev_project_cost_ifrc11_1, ev_project_cost_wri17_1], and WOCAT values are compiler-entered conversions from local currency. The mangrove cost range is extremely wide, and in Tabasco, Mexico, a budget-driven subsidy of US$94.68/ha accompanied a programme the authors judged insufficient for success [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_1]; values from high-income and upper-middle-income settings are excluded from the low and lower-middle income range. The Bangladesh mean is modelled by value transfer from a cost function, not an observed project cost [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].

forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.mechanism: In low and lower-middle income settings, costs are lowest where existing regrowth is used: natural regeneration in Uganda at US$26/ha and assisted natural regeneration in Niger and Bangladesh at US$90/ha and US$197.62/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_5, ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_establishment]. Planting-based work costs more, from mangrove planting with community support in the Philippines (US$211/ha) and Bangladesh to rain forest corridor planting in Madagascar (US$938/ha), community forest management in Benin, broadleaf plantations in India, the Khost learning site in Afghanistan and community microbasin reforestation in Honduras at US$5,402.39/ha [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_4, ev_project_cost_wri17_4, ev_project_cost_wri17_2, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_establishment]. For mangrove restoration in Bangladesh a World Bank study models a mean cost of 7,700 USD/ha across the country [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].
forest_restoration__cost_per_hectare_res.conditionality: The table and cited values give no price year and the WOCAT values are compiler conversions from local-currency entries; Philippine mangrove costs rise to US$1,156.52/ha once preliminary and maintenance activities are included [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_5], so figures that omit them understate full cost. The Bangladesh mangrove figure is a modelled value transfer, not an observed cost, and sits far above the community-supported planting costs [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].

forest_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avoid.mechanism: Abatement cost compares implementation and land opportunity costs with the carbon gained: modelled natural regeneration costs a median of US$23.80 per tCO2 and plantations, net of wood-product revenue, US$23.00 per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_busch24_3, ev_project_cost_busch24_4]. In Colombia's western Andes a median carbon price of US$1.99 per tCO2 over 30 years was enough to compensate landowners for letting pastures regenerate [ev_project_cost_chazdon16_1], and carbon prices of 4.5 to 18.0 US$ per tCO2 could support restoring most deforested mangroves while conserving remaining mangroves needs 3.0 to 13.0 [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_1, ev_project_cost_jakovac20_2]. Two payment schemes report low programme costs per tonne of carbon: the PAS scheme in Brazil was estimated at 0.56 USD per ton of CO2, and the Ugandan scheme cost $0.57 per ton of delayed emissions against an estimated social benefit of $1.11 per ton, roughly two times the cost [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3].
forest_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avoid.conditionality: All units are modelled or break-even prices rather than project budgets, the plantation range runs from negative (profitable without carbon payments) to US$724 per tCO2, and the mangrove conservation figure concerns avoided emissions from protecting existing forest rather than restoration; the Colombian figure is cited from another study and states no price year. The Brazilian figure is a total programme cost given without assessing cost-effectiveness, both payment figures are cited in a systematic review, and both concern paying landholders to keep existing forest rather than restoring it [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3].

forest_restoration__cost_reduction.mechanism: Natural regeneration lowers cost by letting forests grow back on their own or with low-cost assistance, cited at US$12-3,880/ha against US$105-25,830/ha for restoration projects, and is often more effective than full tree planting in long-term success [ev_project_cost_williams24_1]; European guidelines likewise note its lower cost and locally adapted genetic material [ev_project_cost_stanturf26_1]. In a mulching experiment in tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, polyethylene mulch cut the cost of each established plant, including nursery costs, from 18.00 USD on bare soil to 2.45 USD, because 92 of 180 plants established against 10 of 180 without mulch [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. Decentralised administration of Van Panchayat forests in India is associated with costs approximately 1/13th of those under state administration [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].
forest_restoration__cost_reduction.conditionality: Successful restoration can be costly: the black-mangrove restoration cited in Tabasco, Mexico, needed sanitation, dredging, soil conservation works, ridge restoration, staff training, plant production, transplanting and monitoring [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_2]. The European statement is an expert assertion that also notes limits in species composition, and the cost comparison is a cited range without price year. Organic mulches cut cost per established plant less, to 12.50 USD with alfalfa straw and 13.33 USD with leaf litter, and the result comes from a single experiment at one site [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]; the Van Panchayat cost figure is cited in a systematic review and concerns administering existing forest [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].

forest_restoration__cross_family__biodiv.mechanism: A global meta-analysis of 221 study landscapes found that forest restoration enhances biodiversity by 15 to 84% and vegetation structure by 36 to 77% compared with degraded ecosystems, as regrowing forest rebuilds habitat structure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__biodiv.conditionality: This rests on a single meta-analysis in which restored sites are secondary or selectively logged forests and active and passive restoration are not separated, so it cannot attribute the gain to a particular restoration family.

forest_restoration__cross_family__cost_p.mechanism: Across restoration families, the opportunity cost of land is generally higher and more variable than implementation cost, with a modelled median of US$4,807/ha [ev_project_cost_busch24_5]; restoration projects in the tropics and subtropics are cited at US$105-25,830/ha [ev_project_cost_williams24_2] and the TEEB study assumed US$2,390-3,450/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__cost_p.conditionality: These are modelled, cited or assumed values rather than observed project costs, none states a price year, and they pool restoration methods without separating families.

forest_restoration__cross_family__drough.mechanism: A meta-analysis of catchment restoration in Ethiopia reports that exclosures, tree planting, bunds and terraces reduce water losses and improve the quantity and quality of water in soils, rivers and aquifers, a pathway to drought resilience [ev_soil_water_retention_meaza22_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__drough.conditionality: This is a single source on soil and stream water, a component of drought impact rather than a drought outcome, and it pools exclosure and planting with soil and water conservation structures, so the share due to tree restoration is not isolated [ev_soil_water_retention_meaza22_1].

forest_restoration__cross_family__flood_.mechanism: This row rests on a single global systematic review: flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of the studies with data on them, consistent with forest cover slowing storm runoff [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__flood_.conditionality: The review pools explicit and implicit forest restoration with forestry and afforestation, is dominated by temperate and Oceania studies, and reports vote counts rather than effect sizes, so it does not say how large the reduction is or which restoration practice delivers it [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. No unit comes from a low- or lower-middle-income setting. Expert positions point the other way: an FAO–CIFOR synthesis concludes that massive forestation programmes proclaimed as the answer to preventing floods simply will not do the job, although reforestation may bring other benefits [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_3], and a published comment argues that reforestation does not necessarily reduce flooding if soil properties do not recover, river bed morphology does not change and settlements, roads and drains remain [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_5]. Neither is a measurement.
