forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.mechanism: Satellite comparisons of forest gain and loss show that more forest cools the land surface locally in tropical and temperate regions, with the largest cooling where tropical forest cover rose by about 50%, while forest loss warms it [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_4, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_5].
forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.conditionality: The cooling is absent in boreal regions [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_3]. The evidence is a single global remote-sensing study of observed forest-cover change, not of planting or regeneration as such, and land surface temperature is only a proxy for heat stress.

forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.mechanism: Gaining forest cover cools the land surface: forestation lowered annual land surface temperature by 0.18 degC in the tropics and 0.19 degC in temperate regions, and forestation of about 50% in tropical regions led to cooling of 1.11 degC, while deforestation warmed the tropics by 0.38 degC [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_4, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_5].
forest_restoration__cross_family__heat_s.conditionality: Boreal regions showed a null effect [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_3]. The source is a single remote-sensing study of observed forest-cover change rather than a named restoration practice, it measures annual land surface temperature rather than heat extremes, and microclimate buffering enters as a component of heat-stress hazard.

forest_restoration__cross_family__produc.mechanism: Under the Reflorestar payment programme in Espírito Santo, Brazil, the poorest quarter of municipalities saw agricultural value added rise by 8% and the value of agricultural production by about 14% [ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_seixas24_3].
forest_restoration__cross_family__produc.conditionality: The gain holds only for the poorest municipalities; the better-off municipalities showed a 14% decline, and aggregate municipal indicators showed no significant effect. The programme pools standing-forest conservation with regeneration, planting, agroforestry and silvopasture, and municipal production value is a proxy for the farm production gap in an upper-middle income setting.

forest_restoration__cross_family__rural_.mechanism: Restored forests can diversify livelihoods and raise income from timber and non-timber forest products [ev_household_income_iufro20_8]; in Wuqi County, China, the sloping land conservation programme increased local incomes by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times [ev_household_income_wri17_1], and global estimates put the benefit-cost ratio of restoring degraded forest land at 7.5 to 30.9, including public goods [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2]. A meta-analysis of payment-for-environmental-services programmes finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__rural_.conditionality: Restoration can also take agricultural land and reduce on-farm income or employment [ev_household_income_iufro20_7], few studies conclusively show that restored-forest benefits alleviate poverty, which occurs over years or decades when it does [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4], and Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no significant effect on municipal GDP, value added or employment [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1]. The Wuqi gain is ex post without a counterfactual and largely off-farm and subsidy-driven, the benefit-cost ratios are global model estimates, and income and returns are proxies for poverty. The same meta-analysis finds no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11), on nonagricultural income or on household assets [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2], so the income gain does not show up as farm income or wealth.

forest_restoration__cross_family__soil_e.mechanism: Tree roots stabilise slopes: forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and landslides increase as roots decay about three years after clearance, remaining high until regenerating roots mature at around 15 years [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2]. After clear-felling in Alaska, USA, the landslide-affected area was 5 times greater than before logging, and mass erosion on steep terrain can rise two- to more than ten-fold after harvesting [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4].
forest_restoration__cross_family__soil_e.conditionality: During extreme rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity, and for deep-seated failures, forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. The evidence describes forest loss rather than restoration, comes mostly from temperate and high-income settings, is recorded under erosion for lack of a landslide category, and rests on a single FAO review citing other studies and expert consensus.

forest_restoration__cross_family__water_.mechanism: Expanding forest cover tends to reduce water supply downstream: in a global systematic review, annual water yield decreased in about 80% of study cases after forest restoration or other forest cover expansion, baseflow decreased in 63% and groundwater levels or recharge in 67%, and no water-yield gains were observed in the meta-analysed subset [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1, ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1, ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis explains why: tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and trees use much of the water that does soak in, so extensive reforestation or afforestation should not be expected to increase dry-season low flows [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
forest_restoration__cross_family__water_.conditionality: Infiltration increased in 83% of studies reporting it, so soil water conditions can improve even where yield falls, though recovery of infiltration and recharge takes decades rather than years [ev_soil_permeability_filoso17_1, ev_soil_permeability_iufro18_1]; and the larger the temporal or spatial scale, the smaller the decrease in water yield [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]. The review pools forestry and afforestation with restoration, is dominated by temperate and Oceania studies and reports vote counts, and water regulation, recharge and permeability enter as components of water stress.

forest_restoration__drought__all.mechanism: The India compiler credits a programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries with improved surface and subsurface hydrological functioning in the upper watershed, which raised springshed groundwater stores and dry-season stream and spring flows, and the Niger compiler credits assisted natural regeneration with improving vegetation cover and woody production that help reduce the impacts of long droughts in the rainy season [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts]. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than households beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a meta-analysis of Ethiopian catchment restoration reports that exclosures, tree planting, bunds and terraces reduce water losses and improve water in soils, rivers and aquifers [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_soil_water_retention_meaza22_1]. A regional model of large-scale reforestation in water-insecure parts of the Asia-Pacific found fewer extremely dry months in 9 of 15 regions [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__drought__all.conditionality: The Tigray yield advantage was larger in the drier first year than in the following one, and it compares exclosures with open grazing, so it measures a downstream benefit to cropland rather than production on the restored land itself [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3]. The Ethiopian meta-analysis bundles exclosure and planting with bunds and terraces, the India and Afghanistan sheets bundle planting, regeneration and protection, and the WOCAT units are compiler ratings, not measurements, with the Afghanistan compiler rating drought impacts only slightly reduced [ev_soil_water_retention_meaza22_1, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_drought_impacts]. The modelled benefit is landscape-scale only and the source notes that most regional changes were not significant, so it does not speak to plot-scale restoration [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].

forest_restoration__drought__all__income.mechanism: Compilers rate afforestation in Cabo Verde as raising soil moisture and off-site water availability, and afforestation of bare karst land in Bosnia and Herzegovina as slightly improving water availability and water collection [ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1523_2011_soil_moisture, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability].
forest_restoration__drought__all__income.conditionality: This upper-middle-income slice rests on practitioner ratings from very few technology sheets, all of them water proxies rather than a drought-impact rating or measurement. The sheets state no mechanism, so the link from more soil water to lower drought impact is inferred through the proxy, not observed.

forest_restoration__drought_hazard.mechanism: WOCAT compilers report that assisted natural regeneration in Niger reduces drought impacts by improving vegetation cover and woody production, and that broadleaf plantations and assisted regeneration in India improved surface and subsurface hydrological functioning in the upper watershed; the Khost site in Afghanistan is also rated as reducing drought impacts [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2325_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_drought_impacts]. A regional climate model found reforestation reduced the probability of extremely dry months in 9 of 15 regions [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__drought_hazard.conditionality: The field evidence is compiler ratings without measured drought outcomes, and the model unit is a landscape-scale scenario in which most regional changes were not significant.

forest_restoration__fire__all.mechanism: Where compilers rate fire risk as lower, they credit active fire management rather than tree cover: enclosure with fire breaks and bylaws in Tanzania, and villagers guarding the forest from anthropogenic and wild fires in India, where greener cover and less flammable pine-needle build-up lower the risk of burning [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_fire_risk, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_fire_risk]. A World Bank evaluation lists reduced incidence of fires among the environmental outcomes that participatory forest management projects reported where those outcomes were monitored [ev_fire_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__fire__all.conditionality: Ratings point both ways: an area closure in Ethiopia is rated as slightly raising fire risk, and the Uganda tree-planting compiler rates no change while warning that dense forest brings fire risk, already common in a neighbouring district [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_fire_risk, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk]. Apart from the World Bank evaluation, which gives a portfolio-level narrative without magnitudes and covers only projects that monitored the outcome [ev_fire_hazard_ieg13_1], all units are practitioner ratings, and the reduction appears to depend on protection measures being in place.

forest_restoration__flood__all.mechanism: Reforestation slows storm runoff and lowers flood peaks in catchment models: in Slovakia's Hornad watershed a 50% increase of forest cut a simulated flood peak from 84.8 to 74.9 m3/s and reduced peaks by about 24% on average in rain-duration tests, more for short storms than long ones [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and an afforestation simulation for Luxembourg's Alzette basin decreased the peak by 8% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. A systematic review found that flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of studies reporting them [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde, Uganda and Bosnia and Herzegovina, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan, mangrove buffers in the Philippines, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and a learning site in Afghanistan rate downstream flooding or flood impacts as reduced; an Ethiopian compiler notes that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced, and the Afghan compiler that riverbanks were revegetated with communities planting cuttings along banks and shorelines [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
forest_restoration__flood__all.conditionality: The modelled benefit shrinks as rain continues, from 29% for the shortest rain duration to 17% for the longest [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and all catchment results are scenarios of large forest-cover gains in temperate high-income basins; the largest figure, a 42.3% peak reduction from converting all arable land to forest, is a secondary citation with no basin named [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. The review pools restoration with forestry and afforestation and reports vote counts rather than magnitudes [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1], and the low- and middle-income evidence consists of WOCAT compiler ratings, not measured flows or flood damage. Expert syntheses dispute that planting at scale reduces floods: an FAO–CIFOR review concludes that massive programmes of forestation proclaimed as the answer to preventing floods simply will not do the job, although reforestation may have many other benefits [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_3], and a comment on a global flood analysis argues that reforestation does not necessarily reduce flooding, for example if soil properties do not recover, river bed morphology does not change, and settlements, roads and drains remain unaltered [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_5]. forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.conditionality: This is a single observational source; it describes stress at poorly sited plantings rather than measuring how much drought reduced survival, and it points to site selection along the tidal gradient as the controlling factor.

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.mechanism: Compilers judge mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local rainstorms and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping well with local thunderstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1442_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4300_2019_local_thunderstorm].
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.conditionality: Both units are practitioner judgements of good coping, with no observed damage behind the threat class.

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.mechanism: Flooding was among the stress factors observed at all planted mangrove sites in a national census in Sri Lanka, alongside drought, smothering, browsing and cattle trampling [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_3].
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.conditionality: Compilers rate mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with river floods, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping well with storm surge and mangrove buffers in the Philippines as coping very well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1442_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_4300_2019_storm_surge_coastal_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_578_2016_storm_surge_coastal_flood], so the threat is slight and practitioner-rated; the Sri Lankan observation does not separate flooding from the other stresses.

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.mechanism: Rapid sedimentation, as after storms, and excess leaf litter can smother the aerial roots of mangrove trees and cause delayed mortality [ev_establishment_survival_gijsman21_1].
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.conditionality: The evidence is a single review statement on existing mangrove forests with no magnitude; transfer to planted or regenerating mangroves is assumed.

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.mechanism: In Sri Lanka, mangrove seedlings and propagules planted in the low intertidal zone of the wet zone suffered long-term submergence due to heavy rains [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_1].
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.conditionality: This is a single observational source that does not quantify the resulting losses; it points to planting position along the tidal gradient as the controlling factor.

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.mechanism: Mangrove tree damage rises rapidly once tropical-cyclone winds exceed 130 km/h, and extreme events with very high water levels and winds can severely damage or destroy mangrove areas, leaving them less able to reduce surge [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1]. forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__as.conditionality: Compilers judge mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local windstorms and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1442_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm]. A WOCAT mangrove afforestation sheet from Bangladesh reports that plantations create habitat for birds, crabs, wildlife and fish.
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__bi.conditionality: The same meta-analysis found no clear difference in crab or fish production and diversity between restored mangroves and unvegetated tidal flats, and its metric merges production with diversity. The Bangladesh entries are compiler ratings, not measurements.

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__ca.mechanism: Planted mangroves take up CO2 rapidly as the trees grow: a global review of forest landscape restoration ranks mangrove tree planting as the second most efficient restoration type at removing CO2, with the highest rates in the first 20 years and lower rates over the following 40 years. A mangrove meta-analysis also finds higher carbon sequestration in restored mangroves than in unvegetated tidal flats.
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__ca.conditionality: The removal-rate review covers active planting only, and its text and table give slightly different later-period rates; the meta-analysis reports publication bias for carbon sequestration. The Bangladesh WOCAT sheet contributes only a compiler rating of increased below-ground soil organic matter, a component proxy for sequestration.

WOCAT costs are compiler entries converted from local currency, and most units sit outside the lower-middle-income band used for the class. The World Bank figure is a value transfer from a cost function rather than an observed project cost [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__co.conditionality: This is a modelled break-even price from a single global study with no country context, not an observed project cost per tonne; it depends on assumed opportunity and restoration costs and on the share of carbon credited.

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__ru.mechanism: Mangrove planting supports coastal livelihoods mainly through aquatic products: in northern Viet Nam the community mangrove plantation project raised per-hectare yields of shells and oysters and so local income, and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives benefit-cost ratios above unity in every commune, higher when ecological benefits are counted. A global meta-analysis likewise finds mangrove restoration benefits exceed costs, a cited Philippine study concludes the same, and WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh and Senegal rate food self-sufficiency, production risk and long-term returns as improved. Valuations of standing mangroves show what keeping them is worth to coastal households: in Orissa, India, existing mangroves provided house-protection benefits of USD 1218 per hectare in a single super cyclone [ev_economic_return_das11_1], a comparison of costs and benefits found protecting the remaining mangroves there economically justified [ev_economic_return_dasvincent09_1], and in Thailand storm protection accounted for US$ 8,966–10,821 per hectare (~87%) of estimated mangrove value, with the long-term total economic value of an intact mangrove swamp about 3.6 times that of converting it to shrimp aquaculture [ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2].

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__so.mechanism: The Bangladesh WOCAT compiler reports that surface runoff decreased because of canopy cover and sediment accretion in the mangrove plantation, a component of erosion risk. A World Bank modelling study for Bangladesh finds mangrove belts reduce shear stress at the toe of coastal embankments by 7%-16% where they average 60 m wide and by 45%-72% where they average 477 m, which also allows thinner revetments [ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_2].
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__so.conditionality: The pool is one compiler rating of runoff used as a component proxy and modelled shear-stress reductions at embankments from grey literature; there are no measured erosion data for mangrove restoration [ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_2].

forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__wi.mechanism: Mangrove planting in northern Viet Nam is credited with keeping a sea dyke undamaged in a 2005 typhoon of the same level as one that damaged it in 1987, and with cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent; planted Sonneratia mangroves in Hainan, China cut mean wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. A global model credits current mangroves with reducing flood damages from tropical cyclones, and compilers for mangrove buffers in the Philippines and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Studies of standing mangroves show the protection that keeping the forest provides. In Orissa, India, villages with wider mangroves between them and the coast had significantly fewer deaths in the 1999 super cyclone, with 1.72 additional deaths per village within 10 km of the coast predicted had mangrove width been reduced to zero [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_2], and without mangroves the area would have seen 23% more fully collapsed houses [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_1]. In Central America category 3 hurricane winds would lead to a 24% decrease in economic activity where mangrove width was less than 1 km but no damage where it was wider [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_delvalle20_1], and across coastal communities direct cyclone exposure cost 5.4–6.7 months of economic activity at average mangrove extent against 2.6–5.5 months with more extensive mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_hochard19_1]. Numerical models and laboratory experiments support mangroves reducing the water height and velocity of cyclone storm surges, a South Florida model concluded a 7–8 km wide mangrove forest could reduce a category 3 hurricane's surges by ~80%, and in Belize cleared sites lost significantly more field equipment in storms than sites with intact mangrove [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_3, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_4].
forest_restoration__mangrove_coastal__wi.conditionality: The Viet Nam results are uncontrolled before-and-after comparisons attributed to mangroves by evaluators of the implementing Red Cross programme, and the global model concerns existing rather than restored mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_menendez20_1]. The Philippines and Bangladesh units are compiler ratings, not measurements, and the Bangladesh compiler rates only a slight reduction [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Protection weakens where the surge is largest: in Orissa the death-reducing effect was smaller for above-mean storm surges [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_3], and no mangrove effect on fully collapsed houses was visible within 10 km of the coast, where many houses were swept away instead [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_2]. A review finds that observational studies have not given conclusive results on how much protection mangroves provide [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_2]. The Orissa, Central American and global community studies are quasi-experimental comparisons of places with more or less existing mangrove, so they measure the service of keeping mangroves rather than the performance of planted stands, and the Florida surge figure is a model result cited in a review [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_3].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The compiler for an area closure on degraded land in Ethiopia judges the technology as coping well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1598_2014_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This is a single practitioner judgement of good coping, with no observed damage behind the threat class.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: In early succession, regenerating land that is not overseen faces a high probability of fire outbreaks, particularly in dry years, which calls for fire protection and control, and young regrowth forests fail to persist partly through vulnerability to fire [ev_fire_hazard_chazdon16_1, ev_establishment_survival_williams24_1].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: Both units are narrative statements from tropical reviews, unquantified and co-listing fire with market shifts, perverse policies and lack of awareness of the benefits of young forests.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The compiler for an area closure on degraded land in Ethiopia judges the technology as not coping well with general river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1598_2014_general_river_flood].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This is a single practitioner judgement with no description of the damage and no measurement.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The compiler for an area closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia judges the technology as coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1568_2013_local_windstorm].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This is a single practitioner judgement, and the technology mixes closure with planting.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Natural regeneration rebuilds biodiversity as secondary forest develops. Across tropical chronosequences species richness recovers fastest and composition slowest, with richness after 20 years at 78% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_2]; tree species richness in Brazil's Atlantic Forest rises with time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1]; and in the western Andes of Colombia bird and dung beetle communities in regenerating forest came to resemble old growth [ev_biodiversity_outcome_chazdon16_1]. A pantropical meta-analysis finds natural regeneration outperforms active planting for plants, birds and invertebrates [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], an Ethiopian WOCAT compiler rates animal diversity as increased under area closure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity], and in Senegal's southern Groundnut Basin woody species richness in exclosures rose from 27 species after 1 year to 51 species after 5 and 12 years, an increase of more than 52% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: Recovery of composition and endemism is slow: composition after 20 years was only 33% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1], and in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest regaining mature-forest endemism was estimated to take 1987 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. A French review citing a global analysis reports species richness losses after clear-cutting followed by natural regeneration relative to uncut forest, though smaller than under plantations [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_3], the meta-analysis compares regeneration with planting rather than with degraded land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], and the Ethiopian compiler notes that returning wildlife damages crops and livestock [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The Senegal result compares exclosures of different ages at one site rather than exclosures with open grazed land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Secondary forests regrowing on abandoned farmland and pasture accumulate carbon in biomass and soil: global reviews give CO2 removal rates for natural regeneration in its first 20 years, Brazilian Amazon and Atlantic Forest regrowth approaches mature-forest biomass over decades, Colombian regenerating forests reached about half of old-growth carbon stocks, and soil carbon recovers within years and rises after transition to forest. WOCAT compilers in Tanzania and Tunisia rate biomass carbon and soil organic matter as increased and emissions as decreased, citing controlled bush fire.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: Most of the evidence is pantropical modelling and chronosequences in upper-middle-income Brazil and Colombia; above-ground biomass takes decades to approach old-growth values, and the Amazon figure is biomass rather than carbon from slash-and-burn fallows. The global potential estimates assume regrowing forests are allowed to persist, and the Tanzanian and Tunisian entries are compiler ratings.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Natural regeneration is cheap to implement because it relies on regrowth rather than planting: a model across low- and middle-income countries gives a low median implementation cost, and a WRI table of African restoration costs lists natural regeneration in Uganda at a low per-hectare cost.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The model cost is time-discounted over a fixed horizon and restricted to land near natural forest, and the Uganda figure is a single table entry with no price year; only the Uganda figure enters the class, and neither includes the opportunity cost of land.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Because natural regeneration has low implementation cost and accumulates carbon, a global model finds a moderate median abatement cost per tonne of CO2 once implementation and opportunity costs are included, and a Colombian study cites a low carbon price sufficient to compensate landowners for letting pastures regenerate.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: Both are modelled or break-even prices rather than observed project costs: the global estimate is limited to land near natural forest and discounted, and the Colombian figure is cited second-hand from an upper-middle-income Andean setting.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Natural regeneration lowers restoration cost compared with planting where forests can grow back on their own or with low-cost assistance, as stated by a pantropical review and by IUFRO restoration guidelines that also cite locally adapted genetic material.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: These are statements of relative cost from a review and expert guidelines (the latter set in Europe), not measured comparisons, and the guidelines note limits in the species composition that regeneration delivers.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures achieved crop yields 188 to 222 kg/ha higher than households beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the advantage at 586.6 kg/ha of grain after controlling for soil fertility, labour, fertilizer and other factors [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The benefit was more pronounced in the drier first year, shown by a significant negative interaction between land management and year [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3]. All units come from one study of exclosures compared with open grazing in a low-income, semi-arid mixed crop-livestock setting, and the yields are those of downstream cropland rather than of the restored area.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures achieved crop yields 188 to 222 kg/ha higher than households beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the advantage at 586.6 kg/ha of grain after controlling for soil fertility, labour, fertilizer and other factors [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The benefit was more pronounced in the drier first year, shown by a significant negative interaction between land management and year [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3]. All units come from one study of exclosures compared with open grazing in a low-income, semi-arid mixed crop-livestock setting, and the yields are those of downstream cropland rather than of the restored area.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The Tanzania compiler rates bush-fire hazard as reduced in riverine enclosures because of the enclosure itself, fire breaks and local bylaws [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: An area closure on degraded land in Ethiopia is rated in the opposite direction, as slightly raising fire risk [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_fire_risk], so letting vegetation recover without fire management may add fuel. Both units are practitioner ratings.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Compilers judge that closing degraded hillsides and other degraded land in Ethiopia to let vegetation recover reduces downstream flooding, most rating the reduction strong and one noting that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from Ethiopian area-closure sheets, not measurements, so the row speaks to a single country and practice. One closure on degraded lands rates the downstream benefit only slight [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_downstream_flooding].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for regeneration-based technologies in Ethiopia rate downstream flooding as reduced, one explaining that runoff from the treated watershed is highly reduced as vegetation recovers.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings from Ethiopian WOCAT sheets in a low-income setting, with no measured discharge or flood data, so the strength of the effect rests on practitioner judgement.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia report that regenerating enclosed areas mainly raise fodder production, harvested as cut-and-carry grass that in turn supports animal production; some also rate crop production as increased, citing deeper, more fertile soils and mulch made available from the area. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged, and the compiler-rated gains run mainly through fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield; apart from the Tigray study, all units are compiler ratings, not measurements. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Regenerating areas raise income through products sold or used from them: Ethiopian WOCAT compilers cite sales of grass and wood and better land productivity, and rate long-term returns against establishment and maintenance costs as positive or very positive, as do compilers in Tanzania and Tunisia. A forest-and-poverty assessment cites secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest improving farmer income in the coastal Atlantic Forest of Brazil, and a review notes that regenerating forests supply timber and non-timber products for local livelihoods.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The Tunisian compiler rates farm income as decreased and long-term maintenance returns as neutral, even while rating food self-sufficiency as improved. Almost all units are WOCAT compiler ratings, poverty is reached only through income, return and food-security proxies, and the literature units are cited examples or general review statements rather than measured income effects.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Recovering vegetation cover slows runoff and holds soil: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, attributing it to improved vegetation cover, controlled runoff and sediment deposited behind bunds, with one Ethiopian compiler noting soil loss halved within the first years. A global forest-water assessment adds that land abandonment with expanding forest and grassland has in some cases decreased soil erosion. A meta-analysis from Ethiopia finds areas closed for grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The same global assessment reports that abandoned terraced land is particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides, and one Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as worse. Apart from that assessment and the Ethiopian meta-analysis, which measures runoff as a component of erosion, all units are compiler ratings, and some regeneration sheets combine enclosure with physical structures such as bunds, so the share due to regrowth alone is not isolated [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for regeneration-based technologies in Ethiopia and Tanzania rate downstream siltation as decreased, citing less sediment transported, improved vegetation cover with controlled erosion, and sediment trapped behind bunds; reduced sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as increased. All units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data, and some sheets combine enclosure with bunds.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Tanzania and Tunisia rate water quantity and water harvesting or collection as improved, the Tanzanian compiler attributing it to reduced unproductive loss of green and blue water. A meta-analysis from Ethiopia finds baseflow from catchments with exclosures was 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: An Ethiopian compiler rates water quantity as unchanged. The pool is small, the other units are compiler ratings, and the Ethiopian baseflow comparison is against cropland rather than unrestored degraded land [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Compilers for an area closure in Ethiopia and for closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia rate excess-water drainage as improved, without stating a mechanism [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: Another Ethiopian area closure is rated as slightly worsening drainage [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage]. All units are practitioner ratings, and the Tunisian technology includes planting.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The compiler for an Ethiopian area closure rates wind velocity as strongly reduced as vegetation recovers on the closed land [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1414_2011_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating of everyday wind speed; it says nothing about cyclone or storm damage to people or to the regenerating stand.

forest_restoration__production_gap.mechanism: Across restoration families the gain runs mostly through fodder and livestock: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Tanzania, Tunisia, Niger, India, Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan rate fodder and animal production as increased, from cut-and-carry grass in enclosures, planted sand-fixing species used as forage and better grazing management. Crop gains are reported where regeneration improves soils or supplies mulch, and in Niger assisted natural regeneration in fields is reported to raise millet and sorghum output by almost 50%; in Brazil the Reflorestar payments-for-ecosystem-services programme raised agricultural value added and production value in the poorest municipalities. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
forest_restoration__production_gap.conditionality: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, and one Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged; much of the evidence is fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield. The Brazilian quasi-experimental gains apply to the poorest quarter of municipalities in an upper-middle-income state, and the source reports a heterogeneous, negative response in better-off municipalities. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: For broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries under sustainable forest management in India, the WOCAT compiler judges the works to cope well with local rainstorms and thunderstorms but only moderately with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: All three ratings come from the same technology sheet and are compiler judgements, not measurements of damage [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The India compiler judges a village-protected programme of broadleaf plantations and assisted regeneration as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: This is a single practitioner judgement, and good coping here reflects active protection by villagers rather than inherent fire tolerance of the stands.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The compiler for the Khost learning site in Afghanistan judges the technology as not coping well at all with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: This is a single practitioner judgement from a site that bundles several land and forest management practices, with no description of the damage and no measurement.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries under sustainable forest management in India rates them as coping moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: This rests on a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of landslide damage [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.mechanism: Protection and community forest management retain and expand forest habitat. GEF sustainable forest management projects show less deforestation than matched areas without projects [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], and forest cover increased by 8% under community management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate plant and animal diversity as increased under protection [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.conditionality: Most units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction, a component proxy for biodiversity, and the Mexican figure is a before-after comparison with no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. In south-west Madagascar transfers of management to communities were found superficial and unable to stop forest clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and GEF project sites likely exposed to urban encroachment showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]; the GEF evidence concerns existing forest under a bundle of protection and management rather than restoration. Governance effects are uneven: under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], an evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. These governance units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction rather than species, the Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in a systematic review, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__car.mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon in place and lets biomass build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], and WOCAT compilers for community forests in Uttarakhand, India and for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rate biomass, soil carbon and carbon storage as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__car.conditionality: Much of the evidence is forest-cover change used as a component proxy, and the GEF carbon estimate is derived from a model over existing forest rather than measured stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], GEF sites under urban pressure showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], and the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: Costs cover establishing community-managed forest and protection works: compiler-entered establishment costs on WOCAT sheets for an afforested community forest with plantation and fodder nursery in India and for a protected area in Afghanistan, and a WRI table entry for community management of forest resources with sustainable fuelwood production in Benin.
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.conditionality: The WOCAT figures are compiler entries, the Indian one converted from local currency and spread over mixed plantation and nursery areas, and the Benin figure comes from a project database with no price year; these packages include planting and infrastructure, so they are not the cost of protection alone.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: Two payment schemes report low programme costs per tonne of carbon: the PAS scheme in Brazil was estimated at 0.56 USD per ton of CO2, and the Ugandan scheme cost $0.57 per ton of delayed emissions against an estimated social benefit of $1.11 per ton, roughly two times the cost [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3]. A global spatial model estimates the break-even carbon price at which carbon payments would cover the land opportunity costs of conserving most remaining mangroves, avoiding release of their stored CO2 [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_2].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__flo.mechanism: This row describes the flood regulation that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. The same cross-country analysis found flood frequency decreasing with increasing natural forest cover and increasing with non-natural forest cover, so the service attaches to natural forest rather than to tree cover of any kind [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_5]. At the local scale forests and forest soils reduce runoff through enhanced infiltration and storage, and peak flows rise after forest removal in small experimental catchments [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_2]. In Malaysia an analysis with adequate controls for confounding factors found flood risk increased after natural forest was converted to plantation crops and urban land [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_1], in the USA forest harvest was associated with significant increases in peak flows in both small and large (100 - 1,000 km2) basins [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_3], and in Swiss valleys with more than 30% forest snowmelt was more gradual and flooding risk lower [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_2]. forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__flo.conditionality: The service fades with storm size and basin size. Forest soils reduce runoff only in small-scale rainfall events, which are not responsible for severe downstream flooding, and forests cannot stop catastrophic large-scale floods caused by severe meteorological events [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_2]; small to medium peak flows are affected most while the largest events do not change noticeably, and studies in larger basins have not usually found changes after deforestation of up to 50% of the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_3, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_4]; and in the Himalaya tree cutting was not the reason for flooding in the downstream plains [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_4]. The cross-country analysis itself found little evidence that further forest loss changed flood deaths or damage [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_3, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_4], and a reanalysis of its data found the correlation between forest cover or cover loss and flood frequency appears absent, with the degraded-lands fraction accounting for most of the variation [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_1]. The Afghanistan unit is a practitioner rating from a learning site that bundles several land and forest management practices [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rec.mechanism: Recurrent costs are compiler-entered annual maintenance costs per hectare on WOCAT sheets for the community forest package in India and the protected learning site in Afghanistan [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance].
