forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rur.mechanism: Protection and community forest management can reduce poverty through forest income, employment and food from forests. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases [ev_household_income_iufro20_1], and community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand and, in large studies controlling for socio-economic factors, drove poverty reduction [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1]: a meta-analysis of counterfactual studies finds small positive effects of protected areas on local monetary outcomes (g = 0.028) and poverty outcomes (g = 0.117) [ev_household_income_kandel22_1, ev_rural_poverty_kandel22_1], households in the Chitwan National Park buffer zone of Nepal have 19 percent higher per capita income [ev_household_income_kandel22_2], and across developing countries living within 10 km of protected areas with documented tourism lowers the likelihood of poverty by 16.1% and of child stunting by 13.4%, with poverty 8.8% lower near multiple-use protected areas even without tourism [ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_1, ev_food_security_naidoo19_1, ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_2]. Exposure to standing forest feeds children: high forest exposure gives at least 25% greater dietary diversity in sub-Saharan Africa [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_1, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_2, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_3, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_4], child dietary diversity rises with community tree cover across 21 African countries, and in Malawi children in communities that experienced deforestation had less diverse diets [ev_food_security_iufro15_2, ev_food_security_iufro15_1]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent and by 66% for low-income households, consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management raised participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, poorer households compensated for lost land access gained 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1], households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_household_income_gefieo19_1], in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1], non-timber income rose after benefit-sharing at Bach Ma, Vietnam [ev_household_income_ieg18_3], and WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate food self-sufficiency and long-term returns as improved [ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_economic_return_wocat_5243_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rur.conditionality: The pool is divided. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; the GEF forest-management portfolio has a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 [ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, local studies found no effect of REDD+ on material well-being, and an analysis in Indonesia found potentially negative effects [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6]; payment programmes have a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3], and payments had no significant effect on a food consumption index in Mexico [ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1], where the payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Benefits skew to the better-off: in Nepal poor and low-caste households receive much less while bearing more costs [ev_household_income_iufro20_3]; near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests forest income rose by an insignificant 2 per cent and lowest-quartile households lost 6 per cent and 10 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; at Bach Ma benefits were shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Livelihood components often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their livelihood aims, and benefit-sharing around Vietnam's special-use forests averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact [ev_household_income_ieg13_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_2]. Protected-area gains depend on tourism: no child growth or wealth gains were found near protected areas without documented tourism [ev_food_security_naidoo19_2], and the forest-diet effect turns significantly negative in richer communities [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_5]. The protected-area, tree-cover and forest-exposure studies measure what living near standing forest provides, not the outcome of a restoration intervention; the Colombian benefit of $411–1,236 per hectare a year is a carbon valuation, not cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3]; and many figures are secondary citations in reviews or World Bank evaluation estimates without a comparison group.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.mechanism: This row describes the slope stability that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: landslides begin to increase when roots decay at around three years after forest clearance and susceptibility remains high until around 15 years, rates of mass erosion on steep forested terrain can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after timber harvesting, and in southeast Alaska the area affected by landslides after logging was 5 times greater than in a 100-year period before it [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, the Indian compiler noting that trees and other vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis likewise notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil a certain amount of mechanical support, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]. The landslide units are forest-loss contrasts and expert consensus, largely from temperate regions and cited second-hand, so they show what clearing costs rather than measuring the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_2, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_3, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]. The India and Afghanistan units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices. The root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by the presence or absence of a well-developed forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2]. A measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: The Indian Van Panchayat WOCAT compiler rates downstream siltation as decreased because vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff, the component of water quality this row rests on.
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: A single compiler rating of siltation used as a component proxy; there are no measured water-quality data.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate water quantity, availability and harvesting or collection as improved: the Indian compiler cites better soil water-holding capacity from slower runoff and improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, and the Afghan compiler cites water seeping into the ground through revegetation and recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: Globally, standing forest passes a smaller share of precipitation to streamflow than non-forest land, a mean water transmission fraction of 33.8% against 40.8%, so keeping forest can mean less runoff downstream; this is a land-cover comparison, not a protection outcome, and the difference may not hold locally [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_2]. The positive units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices, with no measured flow or groundwater data. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis makes the same point from the other side: replacing forest cover with other land uses almost always results in increased runoff and streamflow [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_2], so keeping forest holds back water that would otherwise reach streams.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.mechanism: The India compiler rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as strongly reduced, explaining that erosion from extreme rain storms is reduced by decreasing flow velocity [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.conditionality: This single practitioner rating describes rain-storm erosion, not wind damage, so it is weak support for a wind or cyclone effect. The programme bundles plantations, assisted regeneration and nurseries with village protection.

forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.mechanism: Recurrent costs are annual maintenance costs per hectare entered on WOCAT sheets for mangrove, regeneration, community forest and other restoration technologies in Niger, Bangladesh, India, Afghanistan, Honduras, the Philippines and Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4300_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_maintenance], plus a WRI table entry for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.conditionality: Values span a very wide range because the technologies and cost items differ, the WOCAT figures are compiler entries mostly converted from local currency, and the WRI figure has no price year [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]; the units from upper-middle-income countries were set aside from the class, which rests on the low- and lower-middle-income entries. The Costa Rican figure is a payment for keeping forest, expressed per hectare of forest that would not otherwise have been there, and is cited in a systematic review rather than drawn from programme accounts [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty.mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases, community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]; in Costa Rica, payments for reforestation made up 18.66% of participants' income, against about 10% of family income in other Latin American programmes [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Mangrove planting in Viet Nam raised shell and oyster yields per hectare, with benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits, and a global meta-analysis gives mangrove restoration benefit-cost ratios of 10.50 to 6.83 [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_su21_1]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes, and plantations would be profitable without carbon payments across 28.3% of the plantation-feasible area [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2, ev_economic_return_busch24_1]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty.conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, the Ugandan compiler rates it unchanged, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, an implementer-commissioned evaluation in Viet Nam, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), perception scores (the Costa Rica economic impact of 63.9%), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2, ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_padilla17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The newer governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) or on a food consumption index in Mexico (0.09 SMD) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2, ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Vietnam's plantation return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and its gains rested on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1], Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh one measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: Restoration and community forest management reach poor households mainly through income, food and fodder. In a rigorous analysis of 18,000 community forests in Nepal, community forest management reduced both poverty and deforestation; community forest management in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on household living standards, particularly for those closer to forests and with more education; and household survey data around GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. The benefits of mangrove reforestation projects were found to outweigh their costs in the Philippines, and a World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. WOCAT compilers in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Honduras, India, Niger, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda and Uzbekistan rate long-term returns on establishment and maintenance costs as positive or very positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1330_2010_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1533_2011_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1607_2014_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_750_2016_costbenefit_establishment_long], and most rate farm income, food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved: the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least and reduces forage deficits so livestock keepers are not forced to sell their animals in the lean season, the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water, and the Ethiopian and Uzbek compilers cite sales of grass and wood and unprofitable land starting to bring benefit [ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1330_2010_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1626_2014_risk_of_production_failure].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: Gains are uneven and sometimes absent. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable for lack of valid alternatives, and the Gelose transfers raised neither community incomes nor the money usable in the area [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]. REDD+ contributions to household income in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, and studies of community forest management in Nepal find poor and low caste households receive much less than well-off households while bearing more of the costs through patrol labour and grazing controls [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. The Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced and maintenance returns as neutral, and the Ugandan compiler rates farm income as unchanged [ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_economic_return_wocat_1568_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income]. Most units are WOCAT compiler judgements on technology sheets rather than household measurements; the Nepal, Madagascar living-standards and Philippines findings are secondary citations in reviews; the Uganda result compares household assets near and far from project sites; and the Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression in grey literature [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Community forest management and REDD+ are forest governance instruments rather than restoration practices, and apart from the Nepal poverty analysis every unit measures income, returns or food security as a proxy for poverty.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: Payments for environmental services raise household income on average: a meta-analysis of payment programmes in low- and middle-income countries finds a positive effect on overall household income (standardised mean difference [SMD] = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: The gain does not come from farming: the same meta-analysis finds no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11, 95% CI [−0.06, 0.29]), on income from nonagricultural sources (0.05 SMD) or on household assets (SMD = 0.04) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2]. Livelihood components of conservation projects often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]. The row rests on a single systematic review with meta-analysis and a single portfolio evaluation; income is a proxy for poverty, and both concern payment and protection programmes for existing forest rather than restoration.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings income gains come from subsidies, payments and forest products: China's Sloping Land Conversion afforestation raised local and off-farm incomes in Wuqi County and encouraged off-farm earnings, community forestry in the Sierra Norte de Puebla, Mexico provides wage labour and profit shares, regeneration with palm-fruit harvest improved farmer income in Brazil's Atlantic Forest, mangrove planting in Viet Nam raised shellfish yields with benefit-cost ratios above unity, and protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand. WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate long-term returns as positive.
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: The Turkmen compiler expects farm income to fall in the first years and the Cape Verde compiler notes reduced land-use options with no gain in food self-sufficiency; REDD+ sites in Indonesia showed potentially negative well-being effects and the Reflorestar payments programme in Brazil showed no significant municipal economic effect. The Chinese gains are subsidy-driven, the Viet Nam ratios come from an implementer-commissioned evaluation, and the Colombian figure is a carbon valuation rather than cash income; this row applies to upper-middle-income contexts only.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. Targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent, tree planting on susceptible slopes can reduce landslide risk, eucalyptus afforestation plots in Calabria, Italy with good canopy gave lower sediment concentrations than plots with little or no tree cover, and China's reforestation programmes reduced soil erosion and sediments [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1, ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa and Asia widely rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased under planting, regeneration and area closure, citing vegetation cover, sediment held upstream and slower flows [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. A World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.conditionality: Forest plantations without understory can increase the kinetic energy of throughfall and soil detachment, and abandoned terraced land can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_2, ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4]; an Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation], and afforestation in New Zealand reduces erosion at the cost of water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]. The Pakistan result combines planting with grazing exclusion, most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, several sheets bundle planting with structures such as bunds or terraces, the measured plot and model evidence is mostly from high-income temperate settings, and the runoff results (including the Ethiopian runoff coefficients) measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Management matters: an FAO–CIFOR synthesis warns of particularly serious erosion in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3]. Governance alone may not show up on the ground: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1], cited in a systematic review.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In high-income temperate settings tree cover reduces erosion through canopy protection and slope reinforcement: eucalyptus afforestation plots in Calabria, Italy with good canopy gave lower sediment concentrations than plots with little or no tree cover, confirming the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1]; reforestation of just 9.3 percent (159 km2) of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment could decrease total landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]; afforestation in New Zealand provides erosion reduction benefits [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]; and reforestation in Slovakia's Hornad watershed is modelled to decrease surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The New Zealand afforestation benefit comes with reduced water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3], the Waipaoa and Hornad results are model scenarios, and the Italian evidence compares well- and poorly-covered plots within an afforested catchment rather than afforested against unplanted land [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1]. The row applies only to high-income contexts and does not transfer directly to low-income settings.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings, planting, area closure and regeneration reduce runoff and the soil it carries. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Uganda, Tanzania, Niger, Tunisia, India, Bangladesh, Tajikistan and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss]: an Ethiopian compiler reports an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years, the Tanzanian compiler controlled soil erosion through vegetation cover, the Indian compiler says trees and other vegetation helped mitigate displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands, and a Bangladesh compiler links lower runoff to canopy coverage and accretion of sediments [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4300_2019_surface_runoff].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: An Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse, and the Tajikistan compiler rates only a slight decrease in soil loss [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements, some sheets bundle planting with structures (an Ethiopian compiler attributes reduced siltation to sediments deposited behind the bund), and the Pakistan result combines planting with grazing exclusion [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5]. The Ethiopian meta-analysis values are runoff coefficients and depths, a component of erosion risk rather than measured soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. One measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1], cited in a systematic review.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: World Bank projects using participatory forest management reported reduced soil erosion among their environmental outcomes, where those outcomes were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: Trees alone do not protect the soil: an FAO–CIFOR synthesis warns of particularly serious erosion in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3]. The row rests on two sources, a portfolio evaluation narrative without magnitudes that covers only projects that monitored the outcome [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1] and a regional expert synthesis making a cited general statement about plantations [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3]; neither measures soil loss.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: China's national reforestation and afforestation programmes increased forest cover with reduced soil erosion and sediment, and WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate soil loss, runoff and downstream siltation as decreased.
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The Chinese finding is a narrative summary of programme outcomes without an effect size, and the other units are compiler ratings; this row applies only to upper-middle-income contexts.

forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for planting, regeneration and protection technologies in Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Cape Verde, India and Bangladesh rate downstream siltation as decreased, citing less sediment transported, sediment trapped behind bunds, improved vegetation cover and slower runoff; lower sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on.
forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as increased. All units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data, and some sheets combine vegetation with physical structures such as bunds.

forest_restoration__water_stress.mechanism: The positive side rests on infiltration, soil water retention and, at large scale, moisture recycling. A global systematic review finds infiltration increased with forest cover expansion in 83% of studies reporting it [ev_soil_permeability_filoso17_1]; in Ethiopia, baseflow from catchments with exclosures was 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]; and a coupled land-climate model projects significant water-yield increases under full reforestation in four regions, including 11.4% on the Loess Plateau–North China Plain and 84.9% in the Irrawaddy basin [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. WOCAT compilers in India, Afghanistan, Tanzania, Tunisia, Niger, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate water quantity, availability or collection as improved, citing better soil water-holding capacity, improved spring discharge in the peak dry season and water seeping into the ground to recharge the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability].
forest_restoration__water_stress.conditionality: Agreement is mixed and the measured evidence often points the other way: in the same review annual water yield decreased in about 80% of study cases after forest restoration or cover expansion, baseflow in 63% and groundwater levels or recharge in 67% [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1, ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1]; native-species plantations aged 25 to 45 years in the US Pacific Northwest produce dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to old growth, afforestation in New Zealand reduces water yield, and some modelled regions show nonsignificant declines [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3, ev_water_regulation_iufro18_4, ev_water_regulation_teo22_5]. The decrease is smaller at larger temporal and spatial scales, the review mostly covers plantation forestry rather than restoration with slower-growing native species, and recovery of infiltration and recharge takes decades rather than years [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3, ev_water_regulation_iufro18_1, ev_soil_permeability_iufro18_1]. Compilers in Ethiopia and Honduras rate water quantity unchanged so far, the Honduras compiler expecting effects only in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity]; the WOCAT units are ratings rather than measurements, the water-yield gains are model projections, and the Ethiopian baseflow result compares exclosure catchments with cropland, not with degraded land before restoration [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]. A global synthesis of paired catchments found that afforestation reduced annual runoff on average by 44% when grasslands and 31% when shrublands were afforested, with proportional reductions even larger for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site, suggesting more severe effects in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4], and an FAO–CIFOR synthesis adds that tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and trees use much of the water that does soak in, so extensive reforestation or afforestation should not be expected to increase dry-season low flows [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1]. The Farley catchments, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, concern afforestation of grassland and shrubland rather than restoration of degraded forest land.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings the positive evidence rests on infiltration and baseflow. In Ethiopia a meta-analysis found baseflow from catchments with exclosures 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and a land-climate model projects a significant increase in water yield of 84.9% in the Irrawaddy basin under full reforestation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. WOCAT compilers in India, Afghanistan, Tanzania, Tunisia and Niger rate water quantity, availability or harvesting as improved [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water]: the Indian compiler says the technologies improve the water holding capacity of the soil by decreasing runoff velocity and cites improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, the Afghan compiler that through revegetation water seeps into the ground, recharging the water table, and the Tanzanian compiler a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water.
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: Compilers for area closure in Ethiopia and reforestation in Honduras rate water quantity unchanged, the Honduras compiler expecting effects of reforestation only in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than flow measurements, several from sheets that bundle planting with other practices; the Ethiopian baseflow result compares exclosure catchments with cropland rather than with the degraded land before restoration [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]; and the Irrawaddy gain is a model projection at basin scale [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. This scope holds no measured catchment evidence of the water-yield losses that afforestation causes elsewhere.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: A global synthesis of paired catchments found that afforestation reduced annual runoff on average by 44% when grasslands and 31% when shrublands were afforested, with proportional reductions even larger for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site, suggesting more severe effects in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Trees use the water: tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and trees use much of the water that does soak in, so extensive reforestation or afforestation should not be expected to increase dry-season low flows [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: These results concern afforestation of grassland and shrubland in paired catchments, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, rather than restoration of degraded forest land, so the size of the loss for restoring native forest on cleared land is not measured here [ev_water_yield_farley05_1]. The row rests on one global synthesis of measured catchments and one regional expert synthesis citing earlier work [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: A coupled land-climate model projects significant increases in water yield under full reforestation potential in the Loess Plateau-North China Plain, Yangtze Plain and Southeast China, as added evapotranspiration feeds back into precipitation, and WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate water availability and collection as improved.
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: The Chinese units are regional model scenarios for mid-century, not measured outcomes of restoration projects, and the compiler entries are ratings; this row applies only to upper-middle-income contexts and does not reflect the water-yield declines reported elsewhere in the pool.

forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.mechanism: The Uzbekistan compiler credits afforestation of degraded irrigated cropland with strong bio-drainage through tree transpiration [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage]. Compilers for an Ethiopian area closure and for closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia also rate excess-water drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.conditionality: Another Ethiopian area closure is rated as slightly worsening drainage and tree planting in Uganda as leaving it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_excess_water_drainage]. All units are practitioner ratings, and only the Uzbekistan sheet states a mechanism, in an irrigated setting.

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.mechanism: Planted mangroves shelter coastal land and infrastructure from typhoon winds and waves: in northern Viet Nam a sea dyke seriously damaged by a storm in 1987 did not sustain any damage in a 2005 storm, which evaluators attribute to the protective capacity of the planted mangroves, and the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed fell from 90 per cent in 1996 to 25 per cent ten years later [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]; behind planted Sonneratia mangroves in Hainan, China, mean and extreme wind speed during typhoons were reduced by 59.4% and 53.2% [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. WOCAT compilers for mangrove buffers in the Philippines, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh, broadleaf plantations and assisted regeneration in India and micro-basin reforestation in Honduras rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as decreased [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.conditionality: The Viet Nam results are before-and-after comparisons between storms with no control site, attributed to mangroves by evaluators of the implementing Red Cross programme, and the Hainan figure is a secondary citation [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. The WOCAT units are compiler ratings, not measurements: the India comment concerns erosion from extreme rain storms and the Honduras comment landslide risk rather than wind, and the Honduras and Bangladesh compilers rate only a slight reduction [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Evidence is coastal and mangrove-dominated; it says little about inland forest restoration.

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Compilers for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh, a programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India, and community reforestation of micro-basins in Honduras rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced; the India compiler attributes this to lower flow velocity reducing erosion from extreme rain storms, and the Honduras compiler to forests reducing landslide risk [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets, not measurements, and none describes reduced wind damage: the explained ratings work through rain-storm erosion and landslides. The Bangladesh and Honduras compilers rate only a slight reduction, the Honduras compiler expecting a greater effect in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Mangrove planting in northern Viet Nam is credited with protecting a sea dyke that a comparable typhoon had damaged before planting, and with cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent; planted mangroves in Hainan, China reduced mean wind speed behind the stand during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. Compilers rate mangrove buffers in the Philippines as reducing cyclone impacts and afforestation in Cabo Verde and saxaul dune belts in Turkmenistan as lowering wind speed, by 20-25% in the saxaul belts [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1529_2012_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: The Viet Nam figures are uncontrolled before-and-after comparisons attributed to mangroves by the implementing Red Cross programme's evaluators. The Cabo Verde and Turkmenistan ratings concern everyday wind, not cyclones, and all WOCAT units are practitioner ratings.
